title: Geometric stalks commute with tensor products and scalar extension on the etale site
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with a geometric point $\bar y$, stalks at $\bar y$ being those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and let $Y_{\Et}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For a ring $R$, a sheaf of left $R$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$ is a sheaf of abelian groups with a left $R$-module structure on every group of sections for which all restriction maps are $R$-linear; sheafification of presheaves of $R$-modules is that of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

1. *(Tensor products.)* Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$. Let $\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G$ be the sheafification of the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal F(U)\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G(U)$, and for $s\in\mathcal F(U)$, $t\in\mathcal G(U)$ write $s\otimes t$ for the image of $s\otimes t$ in $(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)(U)$. Then there is a unique $\Lambda$-linear map $\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}\to(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)_{\bar y}$ with $s_{\bar y}\otimes t_{\bar y}\mapsto(s\otimes t)_{\bar y}$, and it is an isomorphism, natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ and compatible with the associativity, commutativity and unit ($\underline\Lambda\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F$, with $\underline\Lambda$ the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]) isomorphisms on both sides.
2. *(Scalar extension.)* Let $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a homomorphism of rings, not necessarily commutative, so that $\Lambda'$ is a $(\Lambda',\Lambda)$-bimodule, and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of left $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$. Let $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F$ be the sheafification of the presheaf of left $\Lambda'$-modules $U\mapsto\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F(U)$, and write $\lambda'\otimes s$ for the image of $\lambda'\otimes s$ in $(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F)(U)$. Then there is a unique $\Lambda'$-linear map $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}\to(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F)_{\bar y}$ with $\lambda'\otimes s_{\bar y}\mapsto(\lambda'\otimes s)_{\bar y}$, and it is an isomorphism of left $\Lambda'$-modules, natural in $\mathcal F$; for homomorphisms $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$ it is compatible with the identifications $\Lambda''\otimes_{\Lambda'}(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda-)\cong\Lambda''\otimes_\Lambda-$ on stalks and on sheaves.

proof.text: For the tensor clause, let $P(U)=\mathcal F(U)\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G(U)$ on the small etale site, with its restriction maps, and let $P^\#$ be its sheafification. The sheafification comparison induces an isomorphism from the stalk $P_{\bar y}$ to $(\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G)_{\bar y}$, carrying the class of a presheaf tensor section to the germ of its sheafified section.

The stalk $P_{\bar y}$ is the colimit of the groups $\mathcal F(U)\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G(U)$ over $\mathcal N_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{op}}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and this index category is filtered because $\mathcal N_{\bar y}$ is cofiltered [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered] (common refinements by fibre products, equalising refinements of parallel maps). The index is a filtered category, not a directed set, so the directed-set comparison [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-tensor-varying-rings] is not applied; the comparison is checked directly (Stacks Tag 00DD argument). The bilinear maps $\mathcal F(U)\times\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}$, $(s,t)\mapsto s_{\bar y}\otimes t_{\bar y}$, are compatible with restriction, so they induce a $\Lambda$-linear $\psi:P_{\bar y}\to\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ sending the class of $s\otimes t$ to $s_{\bar y}\otimes t_{\bar y}$. Conversely, for germs $s_{\bar y}$, $t_{\bar y}$ represented on $(U,\bar u)$ and $(V,\bar v)$, choose by cofilteredness a neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)$ mapping to both and send $(s_{\bar y},t_{\bar y})$ to the class of $s|_W\otimes t|_W$; by cofilteredness (any two refinements and any two parallel maps are equalised further down) this is independent of the choices and $\Lambda$-bilinear, so it defines $\phi:\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}\to P_{\bar y}$. Both composites are the identity on generators (classes of pure tensors, resp. pure tensors of germs), so $\psi$ is an isomorphism. Inverting $\psi$ and composing with Step 1 gives the map in clause (1), with the stated pure-germ formula.

source.place: Lemma 007K, applied to the pointed etale-neighborhood stalk

proof.text: For morphisms $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$, $\gamma:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ both ways around the naturality square send $s_{\bar y}\otimes t_{\bar y}$ to $(\varphi(s)\otimes\gamma(t))_{\bar y}$, so the tensor-stalk map is natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$. The stalk tensor product is generated by pure tensors of germs and the comparison is fixed on them; therefore its associativity, commutativity and unit compatibilities follow by evaluating the two composites on pure germs and using the corresponding module tensor identities. This also gives uniqueness.

source.place: Lemma 008B, with geometric-point stalks identified by etale-cohomology Lemmas 03PT and 04FM

proof.text: For scalar extension, let $Q(U)=\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F(U)$, a presheaf of left $\Lambda'$-modules, and let $Q^\#$ be its sheafification. By the sheafification-stalk comparison [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-geometric-stalk], $Q_{\bar y}\cong(\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F)_{\bar y}$, and this map is $\Lambda'$-linear since the sheafification map is. The rings need not be commutative, so the commutative comparison [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-tensor-varying-rings] does not apply; argue directly as in Step 2 over the filtered index $\mathcal N_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{op}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered], using the $(\Lambda',\Lambda)$-bimodule $\Lambda'$. The $\Lambda$-balanced maps $\Lambda'\times\mathcal F(U)\to\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}$, $(\lambda',s)\mapsto\lambda'\otimes s_{\bar y}$, are compatible with restriction and give a left $\Lambda'$-linear $\psi':Q_{\bar y}\to\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}$; the balanced map $(\lambda',s_{\bar y})\mapsto$ class of $\lambda'\otimes s$ (independent of the representative, since $\lambda'\otimes s|_W$ and $\lambda'\otimes s$ have the same class) gives its inverse, both composites being the identity on pure tensors. (Equivalently, $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda-$ is left adjoint to restriction of scalars and filtered colimits of left modules are computed on sections.) After inversion this is the map in clause (2): $\Lambda'$-linear, with the stated pure-germ formula, and natural since both ways around the square agree on pure tensors.

source.place: Lemma 008B, change-of-rings form, with geometric-point stalks from etale-cohomology Lemmas 03PT and 04FM

proof.text: For successive homomorphisms $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$, both the stalk comparison followed by the second comparison and the direct comparison send every pure tensor $\lambda''\otimes\lambda'\otimes s_{\bar y}$ to the germ of $\lambda''\otimes\lambda'\otimes s$; the associativity identification of iterated tensor products therefore makes them equal. The same pure-tensor calculation proves compatibility on the sheaves and naturality.
